author: yorickdowne
content:
I looked at the ERC PR. Looks pretty straight-forward. Code changes to ethstaker-deposit-cli to support this look to be small.

I'd like to know when the derivation path can be considered "locked in". My current UX assumption is that with `new_mnemonic` and `existing_mnemonic` as well as `builder` we'll create two keystore JSON, one for BLS and one for leanXMSS seed. Deposit json remains BLS. Offline generation of a registration signature requires the validator to be active and the registration contract to be final, we can wait on that. Just the new keystore for now

author: yorickdowne
content:
The derivation paths are little confusing, because you start with chain ID instead of account. On the one hand it makes total sense. On the other we now have:
`m/12381/3600/<account>/0/0` and `m/5326/3600/<chain-id>/<role>/<account>`. which in practice generates:

`keystore-m_12381_3600_0_0_0-<ts>.json` and `keystore-m_5326_3600_1_0_0-<ts>.json` for validator 0, and then `keystore-m_12381_3600_1_0_0-<ts>.json` and `keystore-m_5326_3600_1_0_1-<ts>.json` for validator 1.

We just need to educate users that for BLS, the validator index is first after 3600, and for leanXMSS, it is last. Not a big deal, and let's not bikeshed too much. Just thinking out loud here.

author: manunlp
content:
I'm in favor of the "from generic to specific" ordering, thus `<chain-id>/<role>/<account>`.
However I also understand the concern regarding the BLS-12381 version. I'm not opposed to change the ordering if needed.

There is 2 ERCs:
- [Post-Quantum Validator Seed Derivation](https://github.com/ethereum/ERCs/blob/master/ERCS/erc-8517.md) (merged)
- [Post-Quantum Validator and Builder Keystore](https://github.com/ethereum/ERCs/pull/2215) (TBR)

(cc <@427491045308235776> )

author: yorickdowne
content: That makes sense to me, and I don't think we need to change the ordering. Having both keystores alongside each other is temporary. Choosing a clear derivation path for leanXMSS "from generic to specific" is the better way
